counters.label: Option A
counters.text: Terms stay at 45 days, no rebate. We will accept early settlement on up to ¥257,200 of this invoice at 0.85%, paid on or before day 2.

spans.text: We will accept early settlement on up to ¥257,200 of this invoice at 0.85%, paid on or before day 2.

counters.rationale: Early settlement at 0.85% is cheaper than financing the invoice on the marginal committed source; the line covers the rest of the near-term gap.
counters.formula: break-even: d/(1−d) < c, c = 10.8417% × 30/365 = 0.8911% → d < 0.8832%; largest whole-5bp rate below it = 0.85%. Face: (near-term need ¥405,000.00 − committed line ¥150,000.00) / (1 − 0.85%) = ¥257,186.08 → up to ¥257,200.00 (rounded up to a whole ¥100, at most the invoice). Cost: discount ¥2,186.20 + funding the rest of the gap ¥841.57 (committed plan: ¥841.57) = ¥3,027.77

counters.send_scope: Sends Option A to the buyer (the reply is simulated); records the agreement, with your approval when it changes terms; runs the funding for any remaining gap within your limits.

counters.label: Option B
counters.text: 55-day terms accepted with a 0.30% price adjustment on future invoices, no rebate.

spans.text: with a 0.30% price adjustment on future invoices, no rebate.

counters.rationale: The price adjustment covers the per-invoice cost of funding the longer terms on the marginal committed source, so the net forward concession is about zero; on current books with these terms the router's committed plan (committed plan: ¥899.51 + ¥2,806.95 = ¥3,706.46) keeps the reserve. The offered 60-day terms fail their own re-check; 55 days is the longest that passes. Re-checked as an offer, its terms leave a shortfall of ¥85,000.00 on day 47, funded by the plan: committed plan: ¥1,570.36 (cannot run today).
